name: Simultaneous Yaniv
summary: Each round, every player secretly chooses at the same time to discard a set of equal cards or to call. Claims on cards others discarded collide, and showdowns score hand sums. The lowest total after a showdown that pushes anyone to 100, or after round 30, wins.

player.meaning: card values held, seen only by the owner
sum of hand, recomputed at setup, at a redeal, and at step 10 (announce); this is what decides whether CALL is offered
copy of the hand shown to all at a showdown; empty otherwise
this round's first choice: CALL or 'discard V', revealed after the simultaneous answer
value V discarded this round (-1 if none); also the value of the one card this player offers
number of cards removed this round
claim on an offered value succeeded
player received the blind card this round
the blind value B, told privately to those who took it
score added at the last showdown

game.meaning: the shoe; draws pick a random element and never remove it, so it is always full
at least one player chose CALL this round
L, the lowest hand_sum at a showdown
number of players whose hand_sum equals L
B, this round's blind card value
set true when a showdown happens in round 30

setup: Every player's total is set to 0 and game.round to 0.
game.shoe is filled with the 54 values: two 0s, four each of 1 to 9, and sixteen 10s.
In one deal operation, each player's hand receives 5 values drawn at random from game.shoe, without removing them from the shoe; each hand is visible only to its owner.
Each player's hand_sum is computed as the sum of their hand, and hand_size is set to 5 publicly.

round.effect: game.round += 1; game.any_call = false; for each player: called = false, first_choice = '', discard_value = -1, shed_count = 0, claim = '', claim_success = false, took_blind = false, blind_seen = -1, revealed_hand = []
messages are gathered simultaneously and then broadcast to all as 'Seat {seat} says: {value}'

round.answer: one of: 'CALL' (only if hand_sum <= 7), then 'discard V' for each distinct V in hand, V ascending
round.effect: set first_choice. An invalid answer becomes CALL if hand is empty, otherwise 'discard H' with H = max(hand). called = (first_choice == 'CALL'); game.any_call = (count of players with called) >= 1; all first choices revealed publicly
when game.any_call: revealed_hand = hand for every player (public); game.lowest_sum = min over players of hand_sum; game.lowest_count = count of players with hand_sum == game.lowest_sum

when game.any_call: for each player, round_score = if called then (if hand_sum == game.lowest_sum and game.lowest_count == 1 then 0 else hand_sum + 30) else (if hand_sum == game.lowest_sum then 0 else hand_sum); total += round_score; if game.round == 30 then game.game_over = true; announce each round_score and total publicly; discards chosen this round are ignored
end the game if game.any_call and (max over players of total >= 100 or game.game_over)

when game.any_call: in one deal operation, each hand is replaced by 5 random values from game.shoe (shoe not depleted), visible only to the owner; hand_sum = sum(hand); hand_size = 5 (public); revealed_hand = []. Steps 8 to 13 are skipped because each carries the condition not game.any_call

when not game.any_call: V = value in first_choice; discard_value = V; shed_count = count of V in hand; remove every V from hand (the cards leave play); announce publicly each player's discard_value and shed_count. Each player offers one card of value discard_value

round.answer: one of: 'BLIND', then 'value V' for each distinct V offered as discard_value by at least one OTHER player, V ascending
round.effect: when not game.any_call: set claim; an invalid answer becomes 'BLIND'
when not game.any_call: for each player with claim 'value V': claim_success = (count of players with claim == 'value V') == 1; if claim_success, append V to hand

when not game.any_call: game.blind_value = one random value from game.shoe (not removed); for each player with claim == 'BLIND' or not claim_success: append game.blind_value to hand, took_blind = true, blind_seen = game.blind_value (told privately)

when not game.any_call: hand_sum = sum(hand); hand_size = length(hand); announce publicly for each player: discard_value, shed_count, claim, claim_success, took_blind, hand_size. B and hand contents stay private

when not game.any_call and game.round == 30: revealed_hand = hand for all; game.lowest_sum = min hand_sum; round_score = if hand_sum == game.lowest_sum then 0 else hand_sum; total += round_score; game.game_over = true; announce publicly
end the game if game.game_over or max over players of total >= 100

ending.condition: game.game_over == true or max over players of total >= 100
ending.decided_by: Each player's standing is their total, and lower is better. The player with the lowest total wins, and players tied at the lowest total share the win (a draw among them).

rules.text: Card values are Joker = 0, Ace = 1, 2 to 10 at face value, and J/Q/K = 10. The shoe holds two 0s, four each of 1 to 9, and sixteen 10s (54 cards).
Every random draw picks a value from the full 54-card shoe; the shoe never shrinks or runs out.
At setup, every total is 0, each player is dealt 5 private cards, hand_sum is their sum, and hand_size 5 is public.
When a player's current hand_sum is 7 or less, 'CALL' is offered first; otherwise it is not offered.
A player is offered 'discard V' for each distinct value V in their hand, in ascending order.
Before the first choice, every player writes one message simultaneously, and all messages are then shown to everyone.
First choices are made simultaneously. An invalid answer becomes CALL if the hand is empty, otherwise 'discard H' where H is the highest value in the hand.
When at least one player calls, all hands are revealed and L is the lowest hand_sum.
When a caller's hand_sum is strictly lower than every other player's, the caller scores 0.
When a caller's hand_sum is tied with or above another player's, the caller scores hand_sum + 30 (Asaf); for example, a caller with 5 tied by another 5 scores 35.
When a non-caller's hand_sum equals L, they score 0; otherwise they score their hand_sum.
When anyone calls, discards chosen that round are ignored.
When a showdown leaves any total at 100 or more, the game ends.
When a call happens in round 30, the game ends after that showdown.
When a showdown does not end the game, every hand is replaced by 5 new random cards, hand_size is reset to 5, and the round ends with no discard, claim or blind draw.
When no one calls, each player removes every card of their chosen value V; the hand may become empty.
When no one calls, each player's V and the number of cards shed are announced publicly.
Claim options are 'BLIND' followed by 'value V' for each distinct V offered by at least one other player, in ascending order; a player is never offered only their own offered value.
Claims are made simultaneously, and an invalid claim counts as BLIND.
When exactly one player claims value V, that player adds one card of value V to their hand.
When two or more players claim the same V, all of their claims fail.
One blind value B is drawn per no-call round; every player who chose BLIND or whose claim failed adds one card of value B and is told B privately.

After claims, hand_sum and hand_size are recomputed, and each player's discarded value, number shed, claim, success, whether they took the blind card, and hand_size are announced; B and hands stay private.
When round 30 ends with no call, all hands are revealed, each player scores 0 if their hand_sum equals the lowest hand_sum and otherwise their hand_sum, and the game ends.
When the game ends, the lowest total wins, and players tied at the lowest total share the win.

offers.question: First choice
offers.options: a seat with hand_sum <= 7: 'CALL', then 'discard V' for each distinct value in its hand, ascending; a seat with hand_sum > 7: only the 'discard V' options; a seat with an empty hand: only 'CALL'

offers.question: Claim choice
offers.who: all players (only in rounds with no call)
offers.options: 'BLIND', then 'value V' for each distinct discard_value offered by at least one other seat, ascending; a value offered only by this seat is not listed

choices.why: The designer suggested 4, which is kept. Claim collisions and Asaf ties need at least 3 rivals' worth of interaction, and above 5 the claim list and the announcements grow long while one player's choice matters little.

choices.what: Talk is a simultaneous poll broadcast to all
choices.why: The rules say messages are written at the same time. Talk earns its place: players disagree over who claims which offered value, so announcing a claim can deter rivals or bait a collision.
The engine ranks highest first, and the lowest total wins.

choices.what: Asaf is tested as hand_sum == L and lowest_count == 1
choices.why: This is an arithmetic form of 'every other hand_sum is strictly greater', using table attributes because players cannot be compared directly.
This records the end that comes from a showdown in round 30, so a single check covers both endings.
A thoughtful player times a call against the public hand_sizes and the claims seen, avoids claiming values that others likely want, and uses talk to steer or bluff about claims.

simplifications.what: Cards are stored as values only, with no suits or ranks
simplifications.why: Only values matter in these rules; J, Q and K are all 10 and the Joker is 0.

simplifications.what: The skip of steps 5 to 11 after a call is done by putting the condition 'not game.any_call' on each later step
simplifications.why: The step list is flat, but per-step conditions express the same skip exactly.

simplifications.what: Draws pick from game.shoe without removing the value
simplifications.why: The source states the shoe is full for every draw.
